content.text:
h02.

**delivery function** — `Post` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (the function that constructs the outbound `POST` request and executes it via `safeClient.Do(req)` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`). `PostAsync` (`webhook.go:184`) just enqueues onto a bounded channel; the queued worker goroutines (`init`, `webhook.go:42`) call `Post`, which is where the HTTP request actually leaves the server.

**protection mechanism** — `safeDialContext` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:59`, installed as the `DialContext` of the shared `safeClient`'s `http.Transport` (`webhook.go:32-37`). At dial time it resolves the target host and rejects any resolved address that is a reserved/private IP via `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:44`), which checks against the parsed reserved CIDR list (loopback, RFC-1918 private, link-local/IMDS `169.254.0.0/16`, and IPv6 equivalents) in `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`. Because the check runs on the actually-resolved IP at connection time, it also defeats DNS-rebinding. 

There is additionally an up-front `ValidateURL` check (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`) applied when a webhook URL is created/configured (scheme must be http/https and must not resolve to a reserved IP), but the enforcement that protects the outbound delivery itself is the `safeDialContext`/`isReservedIP` guard on the transport. (Note: an operator can disable the SSRF guard via the `AllowPrivateIPs` flag, `validate.go:41`.)

<result>This is the Memos codebase (Go). I found both things you asked for. There are actually two layers of SSRF protection.

## 1. The outbound HTTP delivery function

**`Post`** — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`

This is where the HTTP request to the external URL is actually executed. It marshals the payload, builds a `POST` request, optionally adds HMAC-SHA256 Standard-Webhooks signature headers, and sends it via `safeClient.Do(req)` at **line 152**. It reads back a size-limited response and checks the status code.

Supporting delivery plumbing:
- **`PostAsync`** — `webhook.go:184` — enqueues payloads onto a bounded channel (`asyncPostQueue`) for async dispatch; 4 worker goroutines started in `init` (`webhook.go:42-55`) drain the queue and call `Post`.
- Actual callers that trigger delivery: `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43` and `:71`.

## 2. SSRF / internal-address protection

There are **two complementary mechanisms**, both keyed off `isReservedIP`:

### a) Dial-time IP blocking (the strong protection, defeats DNS rebinding)
- **`safeDialContext`** — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:59`
- Installed as the `DialContext` of the shared `safeClient`'s `http.Transport` — `webhook.go:32-37`.
- How it works: on every dial it splits host/port, resolves the hostname via `net.DefaultResolver.LookupHost`, parses each returned IP, and if any resolved IP is reserved/private it refuses the connection (`webhook.go:70-74`). Because the check happens at dial time on the actually-resolved IPs, it also defeats DNS-rebinding/TOCTOU attacks.

### b) Up-front URL validation (at config/create time)
- **`ValidateURL`** — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:62`
- Ensures the URL parses, uses `http`/`https` scheme, resolves the hostname, and rejects any resolved reserved/private IP (`validate.go:71-81`). Called when users create/update webhooks: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74`, `:161`, `:182`.

### Shared core
- **`isReservedIP`** — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:44` — checks an IP against `reservedNetworks`, the parsed form of `reservedCIDRs` (`validate.go:14-23`): loopback `127.0.0.0/8` / `::1/128`, RFC-1918 `10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`, link-local / cloud IMDS `169.254.0.0/16`, IPv6 ULA `fc00::/7`, IPv6 link-local `fe80::/10`.
- **`AllowPrivateIPs`** — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:41` — a global escape hatch; when `true`, `isReservedIP` short-circuits to `false` (line 45-47), disabling *both* protections for self-hosted setups targeting local networks.

There is also a related URL-safety check on signing secrets (`ValidateSigningSecret`, `validate.go:90`) but that is about header-injection, not SSRF.</result>
